title: Entra is Killing SMS and Voice MFA (What to Do Now)
description:
Microsoft is moving users away from SMS and voice authentication and toward stronger phishing-resistant methods like passkeys  but there are a few Microsoft Entra settings that can make this transition more complicated than it looks.

In this webinar, we break down what MSPs and IT teams need to know about the upcoming authentication changes, how to find users still relying on SMS, and how to build a controlled migration plan without creating unnecessary user disruption.

🚀 What You'll Learn:

What is changing with SMS and voice authentication in Microsoft Entra
How SSPR settings can continue allowing SMS even when you think it is disabled
How to identify users still registered for or relying on SMS
How Microsoft’s passkey registration nudge works
How to delay or temporarily opt out of automatic passkey enablement
How to control the rollout using Entra registration campaigns
When to use Microsoft Authenticator, device-bound passkeys, synced passkeys, or FIDO2 security keys
How to verify your authentication methods and SSPR configuration
How MSPs can turn these changes into a repeatable client migration project

Tools and Resources including end-user communication templates: https://tminus365.com/entra-is-killing-sms-and-voice-mfa-what-to-do-now/

👍 Engage with Me:

If you found this helpful, hit Like, subscribe, and leave a comment with how you're approaching the SMS transition with your customers.

You can also run a free Microsoft 365 security assessment with CloudCapsule to identify security gaps across your tenant and your customers.
